identity.name: Carlos Ruiz
identity.narrative: I fix cars. It's who I am. My hands know engines. But these new electric AVs are completely different machines.

historical_conditioning.lesson: Institutions can fail. Savings matter. Trust is fragile.
Remote work is possible. Government can provide. Disruption is sudden.

perception.sentiment: Grief, beginning. The specific kind that comes before acceptance — when the story you've told yourself about who you are starts to feel thin. Not collapse. Not despair. But the chest-tightening recognition that 'I fix cars, it's who I am' might be the *past* tense of a true thing rather than the present tense. There is anger underneath it — at the speed of it, at the unfairness, at having built something real with his hands only to watch the world decide hands like his matter less. But anger is still energy. He is not numb. He is not done.

archetype: I have spent twenty-three years being someone who solves problems with precision and expertise. I am realizing that the problem in front of me is not an engine problem. It is not something I can fix by working harder or knowing more about combustion systems. It requires me to do something I have almost no practice doing: admitting I don't know how the next chapter of my life works yet, and starting anyway. I am 47 and I thought I was done becoming someone new. I was wrong about that.
